trajectory_summary: A warm, self-motivated inbound lead was disqualified within roughly 3.5 minutes based entirely on the rep's read of a Google Maps satellite image, without a single verify-section question asked (homeowner, co-owner, utility, bill, roof age, interest reason). Tracy tried three different location workarounds and was met with a DQ each time; the call ends with her giving up, not the rep resolving the technical question with any on-site or specialist-level assessment.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unconfirmed; based on the transcript this is clearly a DQ call (roof/shade), but the manner of the DQ is the concern — it was rendered off a Google Maps image in under 90 seconds with no qualifying conversation, no bill capture, and no offer to route to a specialist for an actual shade study or to at least gather info in case circumstances change (e.g., tree removal).

observed_outcome.quote: But as of right now, we're we're not able. Yeah. I don't think that's what she's gonna do. Okay. Thank you.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The call ends with the customer accepting the rep's conclusion that none of the three proposed locations (main roof, detached garage, side yard) will work for solar given the tree coverage, and no appointment is set.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The call never reached bill collection — the rep disqualified the lead on shade/roof grounds within the first two minutes, before any verify-section questions including bill amount were asked.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked Tracy what interested her in solar. Tracy volunteered that she had just been researching solar companies and Ion was the fastest to call her back, but this is a lead-source observation, not a stated motivation, and the rep did not explore it.

script_coverage.quote: Well, yeah. So I actually work with our design team. I help get the solar designs created for the homes and everything.
I got your address here as 11216 Bro Brooks Spring Road in Ashland, Virginia. Is that correct?

primary_coaching_focus.topic: DQ delivered before any qualification, on unreliable evidence
primary_coaching_focus.quote: So to be honest, Tracy, I do think that you don't have enough sun for solely for solar to work for you, unfortunately.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This is the single most consequential moment on the call: a warm, self-motivated inbound lead was disqualified in the first 75 seconds using a satellite image the rep himself later admits is obscured by the very trees in question, with zero verify-section questions asked. The manager should review whether reps are trained to at least gather basic qualifying info (bill, utility, interest reason) before rendering a shade DQ, and whether a live/specialist shade assessment should be the standard instead of a Google Maps guess.

key_moments.quote: So to be honest, Tracy, I do think that you don't have enough sun for solely for solar to work for you, unfortunately.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep renders a hard-sounding DQ within the first 75 seconds of the call, before any verify-section item is confirmed, based solely on a satellite image read. This is a fast, confident DQ on a thin evidentiary basis (an admittedly obscured aerial photo) rather than a documented protocol for shade/tree DQs.

key_moments.quote: It's just kinda hard to see because on Google Maps, all the trees are in the way.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep admits the tool he's using to make the DQ decision (Google Maps aerial imagery) is obscured by the very trees in question, yet proceeds to use it as the basis for the disqualification anyway rather than flagging uncertainty or offering a live assessment.

key_moments.quote: I was looking at we have a a detached garage. Okay. Is that possible to put it out there at the garage?
key_moments.stewart_read: Tracy is actively problem-solving to make solar work on her property, offering a detached garage as an alternative site. This is a highly engaged customer generating her own solution paths rather than accepting the first no.

key_moments.quote: Kind of the same thing. I do think that you have too much shade. These solar panels, they need as much sun as they can get.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rather than exploring specifics (how many hours of direct sun the garage gets, its orientation, or offering a professional shade study), the rep repeats a generic solar-panel-sun-need explanation and closes the option. No question was asked back to Tracy to gather any real data about the garage's exposure.
